attachment_mechanism.mechanism: kernel-side APFS firmlink/graft namespace composition at mount time (not a plain second mount, not a loop device, not overlayfs)
components: firmlink EA com.apple.fs.firmlink marks directories that are transparently resolved to the paired volume
graft EAs com.apple.fs.graft-vol-uuid / graft-jobj-id-base / graft-jobj-id-len bind a grafted directory tree to a specific APFS volume UUID and inode base (dir_dedupe.c)
mount-time stitch is controlled by com.apple.private.apfs.force-firmlink-stitch; without firmlinks the kernel logs 'mount no firmlinks' and the entitlement forces 'mount force firmlinks'

the stitch reads the sealed-volume FEXT tree and integrity object (logs 'failed to fetch the fext tree' / 'failed to fetch the integrity object') - exactly the fext_tree_oid 61503 and integrity_meta_oid 1289 proven on the SystemCryptex APSB
excluded_mechanisms: plain directory presence (rejected by reviewer rules; not used as proof)
simple loop-device mount of the cryptex as a root filesystem

attachment_timing.phase: kernel mount path (APFS root/system mount) for the firmlink stitch; the Cryptex boot object itself is verified at boot by iBoot (CHIP_CRYPTEX1_BOOT_AP_VERIFICATION)
ordering_dependencies: 1. root filesystem availability (base System volume mounts first)
2. Preboot volume available (DT fstab preboot-vol at /private/preboot)
3. Cryptex volume verified by iBoot cryptex1 boot policy
4. kernel APFS mount-time firmlink/graft stitch composes Cryptex /System + /usr over the base
5. launchd starts; cryptexd manages cryptex assets (post-boot maintenance path)
6. Data volume attachment is a separate later stage (NOT solved here)
attachment_timing.cryptexd_timing_note: cryptexd is a userspace daemon for cryptex asset management; the mount-time firmlink stitch is kernel-side. Both are current-build actors but at different phases.
